records.Concise description: Casey Rodarmor’s fungible-token protocol for etching, minting, and transferring Rune balances through Bitcoin transactions interpreted by Runes-aware software.
records.Deeper researched summary: Runes defines application-layer rules for creating and moving fungible token balances using runestones embedded in Bitcoin transaction outputs. The current Ordinals Handbook states that the protocol does not have a separate prose specification: the `ord` reference implementation is normative. Runestones are carried in an `OP_RETURN OP_13` output and may encode an etching, mint, pointer, and transfer edicts. Rune properties such as name, divisibility, symbol, premine, and mint terms are fixed at etching. Rune state is derived by software that implements these rules; Bitcoin consensus validates the underlying transactions and scripts but Bitcoin Core does not maintain Rune balances.
Creators / founders: Casey Rodarmor — creator of Runes and the Ordinals/ord project
records.Launch / history: Runes activated at Bitcoin block 840,000 in April 2024, the fourth Bitcoin halving block. The protocol was developed within the `ord` codebase as a simpler fungible-token design for Bitcoin transactions.
records.Why it matters in the Runes ecosystem: Runes is the technical substrate for every canonical Rune asset in this registry and establishes the terminology and state-transition rules that wallets, indexers, marketplaces, and applications implement.
Important technical or cultural characte: Etching fixes name, divisibility, symbol, premine, and optional mint terms
Edicts allocate Rune amounts to transaction outputs
Malformed runestones become cenotaphs with protocol-defined burn/unmintable behavior
Application-layer/reference-implementation state, not a Bitcoin Core consensus balance system
Spacers are display/readability markers and do not change name uniqueness
records.Verification basis: Current Ordinals Handbook and current `ord` repository define the protocol and confirm that `ord` is the normative reference implementation.
Research notes / uncertainties: MSC public copy must distinguish Runes protocol/indexer state from Bitcoin consensus state.
Do not imply that Bitcoin Core tracks Rune balances or validates Rune-specific semantic state.
Protocol behavior can evolve with the reference implementation; technical copy should be reverified before publication.

records.Concise description: The protocol-defined genesis Rune, hard-coded as Rune #0 with artificial ID `1:0` and an open mint spanning the Runes activation era.
records.Deeper researched summary: UNCOMMON•GOODS is a special hard-coded Rune in the `ord` implementation rather than an ordinary user etching. Ordinal/Runes sources identify it as Rune #0 with artificial ID `1:0`. Its name is also used in the official Runes documentation to demonstrate spacer behavior. Current ordinals.com state shows a zero premine, divisibility 0, symbol `⧉`, and mint terms that begin at block 840,000 and end at block 1,050,000; the mint remains protocol-defined for that block window subject to its cap.
Creators / founders: Casey Rodarmor / `ord` project — protocol-defined hard-coded genesis Rune
records.Launch / history: Defined before Runes activation as the genesis Rune and made mintable beginning at block 840,000. Unlike ordinary Runes, its identity is hard-coded by the reference implementation.
records.Why it matters in the Runes ecosystem: It is the protocol’s genesis asset and a useful teaching case for the difference between protocol-defined state and ordinary etchings.
Important technical or cultural characte: Name displayed with spacers as UNCOMMON•GOODS
Protocol-defined mint window from block 840,000 to block 1,050,000
records.Verification basis: Protocol documentation/reference implementation plus current ordinals.com Rune state support identity, special genesis treatment, and mint terms.
Research notes / uncertainties: Because this is hard-coded protocol state, ordinary creator/project framing is misleading; describe it as protocol-defined.
Mint completion/status is time-sensitive until its mint window or cap closes and should be rechecked before public copy.

records.Concise description: Rune #1, etched in the Runes activation block and widely treated as the first ordinary public Rune after the protocol-defined genesis asset.
records.Deeper researched summary: Z•Z•Z•Z•Z•FEHU•Z•Z•Z•Z•Z occupies Rune #1 with ID `840000:1`, immediately after the protocol-defined UNCOMMON•GOODS entry. Current on-chain/indexed state shows a fixed supply of 111,111,111 units, including a 110,000,000-unit premine and a completed one-time mint structure. Its primary MSC significance is historical provenance in block 840,000 rather than a currently verified project operation.
Creators / founders: Creator/operator attribution not sufficiently verified from first-party evidence
records.Launch / history: Etched in block 840,000 as Rune #1 / ID `840000:1` at Runes activation. Its mint is complete.
records.Why it matters in the Runes ecosystem: It is the earliest ordinary Rune ID after the special genesis entry and documents the competitive block-840,000 launch cohort.
Important technical or cultural characte: Etched in the Runes activation/halving block
records.Verification basis: Current ordinals.com Rune state verifies the on-chain/indexed identity and launch position. First-party creator/project evidence was not strong enough to support an ACTIVE project profile.
Research notes / uncertainties: Historical significance is the basis for inclusion; secondary-market activity must not be used to upgrade lifecycle.
Supply figures are derived from current Runes-aware index state and should be rechecked if published.

records.Concise description: Rune #2, a block-840,000 project-backed asset associated with CyberKongz and a holder-distribution launch.
records.Deeper researched summary: DECENTRALIZED is an early Runes activation-block asset identified as Rune #2 / ID `840000:2`. Contemporary reporting tied the launch to CyberKongz and described a fully premined 21-billion-unit supply intended for holder/community distribution. MSC includes it for its unusually early Rune number and identifiable project provenance, not for current market rank. Current meaningful operation of the Rune as a standalone project was not verified strongly enough for ACTIVE status.
Creators / founders: CyberKongz — project associated with the launch; individual Rune etcher attribution not independently locked
records.Launch / history: Etched in block 840,000 as Rune #2. Launch-era reporting connected the fully premined allocation to CyberKongz and a holder-distribution phase.
records.Why it matters in the Runes ecosystem: It is one of the first project-backed Runes in the activation block and shows how established NFT/Ordinals-adjacent communities used Runes for distribution at launch.
Important technical or cultural characte: 21 billion-unit launch supply reported as fully premined
records.Verification basis: On-chain/indexed identity is combined with launch-era project/reporting evidence linking the Rune to CyberKongz. Current standalone project lifecycle was not verified.
Research notes / uncertainties: Do not treat an exchange listing or current trading as proof of ACTIVE lifecycle.
The exact distribution execution should be described as launch-era/project reporting unless a first-party archival source is recovered.
Individual etcher attribution is not locked.

records.Concise description: Rune #4, an activation-block asset historically associated with the RUNIX/RuneChain-BVM ecosystem.
records.Deeper researched summary: THE•RUNIX•TOKEN was etched in block 840,000 as Rune #4 / ID `840000:6`. Current Runes-aware state shows a 21-billion-unit fully premined supply, divisibility 18, and symbol `ᚱ`. Historical ecosystem references associate RUNIX with RuneChain/BVM, but this research pass did not verify sufficiently current first-party stewardship of the canonical Bitcoin Rune itself. Wrapped or bridged representations on other systems are not treated as the canonical Rune.
Creators / founders: Historical RUNIX / RuneChain-BVM ecosystem; individual canonical Rune etcher attribution not locked
records.Launch / history: Etched in the Runes activation block as Rune #4. Later ecosystem usage connected RUNIX branding to RuneChain/BVM and wrapped/bridged environments.
records.Why it matters in the Runes ecosystem: Its early activation-block provenance and infrastructure-linked history distinguish it from anonymous early-number assets that have only market presence.
records.Verification basis: On-chain/indexed state verifies the asset and activation-block provenance. Historical ecosystem association is credible, but current first-party stewardship of the canonical Bitcoin Rune was not sufficiently verified.
Research notes / uncertainties: Lifecycle remains UNCERTAIN; do not infer ACTIVE status from wrapped-token or exchange activity.
Do not conflate canonical Bitcoin Rune balances with representations bridged or wrapped on other networks.

records.Concise description: Rune #6, an activation-block public Rune using the SATOSHI•NAKAMOTO name and a completed open-mint structure.
records.Deeper researched summary: SATOSHI•NAKAMOTO was etched in block 840,000 as Rune #6 / ID `840000:22`. Current Runes-aware state shows a 21-million-unit supply, a 4.2-million-unit premine, divisibility 8, and a completed mint that produced the remaining supply in fixed 100-unit mints. The Rune is historically notable for an early activation-block position and culturally resonant name, but reliable first-party evidence for its creator/operator and current project stewardship was not established.
records.Launch / history: Etched in block 840,000 as Rune #6. Its open mint completed after 168,000 mints of 100 units, alongside a 4.2-million-unit premine.
records.Why it matters in the Runes ecosystem: It is an early activation-block Rune with a deliberately high-salience Bitcoin name, useful for documenting the naming competition and launch dynamics around block 840,000.
records.Verification basis: Current ordinals.com Rune state verifies core protocol fields and launch position. Creator identity and current project operation were not established from strong first-party evidence.
Research notes / uncertainties: The name does not imply any connection to Bitcoin creator Satoshi Nakamoto.
Lifecycle is UNCERTAIN; market activity is not lifecycle evidence.
